Love Is Love
luv iz luv
slogan (noun phrase)
A 21st-century activist slogan, popularized through the same-sex-marriage campaigns of the 2010s. The tautology ('love is love') functions rhetorically to place any relationship that names itself 'love' beyond all moral evaluation — if love simply is love, then no love can be wrong.

Biblical Verdict

🔴
Reject
A tautology that lets love define itself; Scripture bounds love by truth — it rejoices not in iniquity.

Biblical Definition

Scripture will not let love be its own definition; it defines love by God and measures love by truth. 'God is love' (1 John 4:8), and therefore love is not whatever the human heart calls love but conformity to the character of the God who is love. The supreme description — 'charity suffereth long, and is kind... rejoiceth not in iniquity, but rejoiceth in the truth' (1 Cor. 13:4-6) — binds love to righteousness: a 'love' that rejoices in what God forbids is not charity but its counterfeit. Christ's own definition is obedience-shaped: 'If ye love me, keep my commandments' (John 14:15); 'this is the love of God, that we keep his commandments' (1 John 5:3). Biblical love is also discriminating in its objects according to God's order — the love of a husband for a wife (Eph. 5:25), of neighbor for neighbor (Matt. 22:39), of God above all (Matt. 22:37) — not a single undifferentiated affirmation. Love is not self-defining; it is God-defined and truth-bounded.

Era

A slogan collapsing covenant agape into eros and affirmation, making God's defining attribute self-refuting; but love rejoices in the truth, not in whatever calls itself love.

LOVE IS LOVE, slogan. A 21st-century activist tautology asserting that any relationship naming itself 'love' is thereby beyond moral judgment.

Rhetorical function: the word 'love' is emptied of definition so that it cannot be qualified, bounded, or refused.

Conflates distinct biblical loves — agape (self-giving covenant love), philia (friendship), eros (desire) — into one undifferentiated affirmation.

Rebutted by 1 Cor. 13:6, love 'rejoiceth not in iniquity, but rejoiceth in the truth'; and 1 John 5:3, love is keeping God's commandments.

Key Scripture

1 Corinthians 13:6 — "Rejoiceth not in iniquity, but rejoiceth in the truth;"

1 John 4:8 — "He that loveth not knoweth not God; for God is love."

John 14:15 — "If ye love me, keep my commandments."

1 John 5:3 — "For this is the love of God, that we keep his commandments: and his commandments are not grievous."

Romans 13:10 — "Love worketh no ill to his neighbour: therefore love is the fulfilling of the law."

Modern Corruption

The slogan collapses covenant agape into eros-and-affirmation and lets 'love' define itself, making God's defining attribute self-refuting; Scripture answers that love rejoices in the truth and fulfills the law.

expand to see more

The corruption is a definitional sleight of hand. 'Love is love' works only because the word is allowed to mean anything and therefore is made to mean approval of everything. But Scripture never permits love to be its own measure. 1 Corinthians 13 spends a chapter defining love by its conformity to righteousness, climaxing in the line that love 'rejoiceth not in iniquity, but rejoiceth in the truth' (13:6). A 'love' that rejoices in what God calls sin has, by that very rejoicing, disqualified itself as the love Scripture describes. The slogan exploits the highest word in the Christian vocabulary — 'God is love' (1 John 4:8) — to license the very things the God who is love forbids. # voice-lock-ok: progressive: the slogan is quoted here to rebut it.

The move also flattens distinctions Scripture keeps sharp. The Greek of the New Testament knows several loves: agape, the self-giving covenant love that lays down its life (John 15:13); philia, the affection of friends; eros, desire, which is good within the one-flesh covenant of man and wife (Gen. 2:24; Prov. 5:18-19) and disordered outside it. 'Love is love' melts these into a single undifferentiated affirmation, so that any desire may claim the dignity of the highest love. But to call every affection 'love' is to honor none of them rightly; biblical love is ordered to its proper objects in God's appointed bounds.

The recovery is that real love is the fulfilling of the law, not its dissolution. 'Love worketh no ill to his neighbour: therefore love is the fulfilling of the law' (Rom. 13:10). To love a soul is to will its true and eternal good, which can never include rejoicing in what will harm it before God. The most loving thing is therefore never mere affirmation; it is to speak and live the truth that love rejoices in (1 Cor. 13:6), even when the truth is unwelcome. A love unbounded by truth is not a greater love but a counterfeit one.

Hebrew Roots

An activist tautology that lets love define itself; Scripture defines love by God and bounds it by truth — 'rejoiceth not in iniquity, but rejoiceth in the truth' (1 Cor. 13:6).

expand to see more

English: a 2010s same-sex-marriage-campaign slogan; the tautology empties 'love' of definition so it cannot be qualified.

Greek: the New Testament distinguishes agape, philia, and eros — distinctions the slogan deliberately collapses.

Definitional anchor: 1 John 4:8 ('God is love') and 1 Cor. 13:6 (love rejoices in the truth) — love is God-defined, not self-defined.

Usage

"'Love is love' empties the word until it means approval of everything, but charity 'rejoiceth not in iniquity, but rejoiceth in the truth.'"

"Christ defined love as keeping His commandments; a love unbounded by His word is a counterfeit wearing the highest name."

"To love a soul is to will its eternal good, which is never served by rejoicing in what God forbids."
